title: How To Handle Needy, Grabby, Dependent Students udents/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin addresses the disruptive pattern of needy, attention-demanding students who interrupt, tattle, and dramatize to get immediate teacher response. He argues these behaviors, while stressful, are not difficult to correct with the right response. His three-part approach: don't lean down to a needy student's level, since doing so communicates that the interruption worked and reinforces the pattern; don't respond immediately, giving the student a pause to reconsider a more mature approach before escalating with a genuine emergency response only if warranted; and don't show excessive concern, since needy students often exaggerate minor issues and validating that tendency deepens dependency. He notes that unchecked neediness spreads to affect every lesson and routine, making a classroom more stressful overall, but that the fix is straightforward if a teacher can resist the natural urge to coddle and instead consistently apply these boundaries.
points: Needy, attention-demanding student behavior is stressful but can be eliminated with a consistent, boundary-setting response.
Leaning down to a needy student's level reinforces and encourages more of the same interrupting behavior.
Pausing before responding gives students a chance to reconsider and choose a more mature approach to communicating.
Showing excessive concern for exaggerated problems validates and deepens a student's dependency over time.
Unchecked neediness, if left unaddressed, spreads to affect every lesson, activity, and routine in the classroom.
quotes: When you lean down toward needy students, you encourage their behavior. You encourage more drama and more interruptions in the future.
In the immediate moments following their interruption, it’s important that you don’t respond. It’s okay to look in their direction to let them know you hear them, but refrain from opening your mouth.
Give them a chance to catch themselves, to rethink their behavior, to consider a more mature and polite way of speaking to you.
This tendency will only worsen if you validate their behavior. It will only worsen if you stop what you’re doing, allow them to interrupt you, and show concern.
The level of dependency in your classroom is directly related to how you respond to it.
They will turn your students into doers and problem-solvers, independent learners and lean-in listeners. They will build confidence and competence and even strengthen character.
